result_semantic_payload.summary: No evidence of fraud-related financial activity was found in the analyzed content. The entire captured corpus consists of three small plaintext files (185, 165 and 166 bytes) plus three matching FILE_CREATED timeline events; no other files, no deleted files, no Windows registry, event-log, prefetch, Amcache, shell-history, browser, email or network artefacts were present in the source scope. Content review shows: /notes.txt is a 2024-05-06 department meeting note explicitly stating "No financial transactions were discussed"; /expense_policy.txt is a generic company expense reimbursement policy v3 (receipts within 30 days, manager approval above 5000 CNY, payments every Friday) with no transactions, amounts, names or receipts; /docs/travel_reimbursement_form.txt is an explicitly blank sample template with no personal data, no amounts and no signatures. The three files were created within a 9-second window (timestamps 1790556664 and 1790556673) in a single FILE_CREATED cluster, which is consistent with a synthetic/bulk drop rather than organic user activity, but this timing pattern alone is not probative of fraud. Conclusion: the available content is neutral administrative/policy material; it neither supports nor refutes fraud. Critically, absence of fraud indicators here is NOT evidence of innocence — the scope is far too narrow (no OS telemetry, no financial records, no user artefacts) to draw any negative conclusion about financial conduct on this device.
